title.narrative: CO-water and hygiene support in Gaza

description.narrative:
The Gaza Strip faces an unprecedented humanitarian crisis following 2 years of genocide, with over 70% of WASH facilities in northern Gaza non-operational. The 10th of October, 2025 ceasefire has triggered massive population returns to Gaza City and North Gaza, where infrastructure is severely damaged or destroyed. Returnees and IDPs find themselves in areas with no functioning water networks, forcing reliance on expensive and limited water trucking. The destruction of water infrastructure, combined with fuel shortages and lack of supplies, has created critical public health risks. Communities face acute water scarcity with consumption below emergencythresholds, inadequate sanitation facilities, and extremely limited access to basic hygiene items. The situation is particularly dire for vulnerable groups including women, children, elderly, and persons with disabilities who struggle to access the limited water points available. This intervention responds to immediate life-saving needs while longer-term infrastructure rehabilitation efforts are planned.
Recent assessments indicate critical humanitarian needs among returnees and host communities in Gaza City and North Gaza .Over 70% of WASH facilities remain non-operational due to extensive damage, with water supply mainly reliant on trucking from limited wells reaching only a fraction of the population. Water consumption has fallen below WHO emergency standards of 15 liters perperson per day, with many families receiving less than 5 liters . The absence of functional water infrastructure forces families topurchase water at inflated prices, depleting already exhausted financial resources. Hygiene conditions have deteriorated drastically, with limited access to soap, sanitary materials, and basic hygiene items increasing disease transmission risks. Women and girls face particular challenges accessing menstrual hygiene materials, compromising their dignity and health. Children are especially vulnerable to waterborne diseases due to poor water quality and inadequate hygiene practices. The lack of proper water storage containers forces families to use contaminated vessels, further compromising water safety. Immediate water trucking and hygiene kit distribution are essential to prevent disease outbreaks and excess mortality. This intervention will provide 6 liters of safe drinking water per person per day for 60 days to 7,400 individuals and essential WASH supplies to 2,000 families, addressing the most urgent needs while infrastructure rehabilitation efforts progress.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
